name: Basilica of St. Francis Xavier, Dyersville
history: A parish was founded in 1859 for German immigrants to Dyersville, with its first church finished in 1862. Its large Gothic Revival successor was begun in 1887, the cornerstone laid in 1888, and dedicated on 3 December 1889; special trains brought people from across Iowa. It was consecrated in the mid-1950s and named a basilica in 1956.
arch: Ruskinian Gothic Revival in brick by Fridolin Heer of Dubuque. Its twin steeples are 212 feet tall with 14-foot crosses, visible for miles across the farmland.
features: The pastor had the altar set on solid rock, a requirement for consecration.
Small gold crosses mark the twelve places where the walls were anointed at the consecration.

look.d: Twelve gold crosses mark the consecration anointings inside.

fun: Dyersville is also home to the Field of Dreams movie site.
journal: Twin spires so tall that pilots steer by them. Iowa farmland all around.

quiz.q: What did the pastor set the altar on?
Who uses the steeples as landmarks?
